title: Underwood (2014): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the answer that best preserves the article's study designs, findings, and limits of interpretation.

items.prompt: What gives the Lothian Birth Cohort studies an unusually early baseline?
options: MRI scans collected from every participant at birth
Archived cognitive test scores from age 11
Follow-up participation by every Scottish survey respondent
Recruitment limited to older adults with diagnosed dementia
items.answer: Archived cognitive test scores from age 11
items.explanation: The recovered Scottish Mental Survey records provide a rare childhood measure against which later-life cognition can be interpreted.

items.prompt: What does the figure of roughly 160,000 refer to in the recruitment account?
options: Older adults who completed MRI scans in the follow-up study
Surviving members of both birth cohorts living in Scotland in 2014
Children tested in the 1932 and 1947 national surveys
DNA samples supplied by the Lothian team to ENIGMA
items.answer: Children tested in the 1932 and 1947 national surveys
items.explanation: The figure describes the original survey participants, not the later Lothian sample of 1,641. Financial constraints prevented researchers from recontacting all surviving survey participants.

items.prompt: How should the finding that age-11 scores predicted about 50% of age-77 IQ variance be interpreted?
options: Childhood scores were related to a substantial share of later-life individual differences
Exactly half of every person's intelligence was permanently fixed at age 11, irrespective of later experience
The mean IQ of the cohort fell by precisely half between the two assessments
All differences in later-life IQ were explained, leaving no role for other factors
items.answer: Childhood scores were related to a substantial share of later-life individual differences
items.explanation: This is a group-level statement about variation among people. It does not mean that half of each individual's intelligence is fixed, and about half of the variance remains unaccounted for by childhood IQ.

items.prompt: What happened to the apparent cognitive benefit of wine consumption after adjustment for childhood IQ?
options: It doubled after the childhood measure was added
It disappeared after childhood IQ was taken into account
It proved that wine directly causes cognitive decline
It remained identical in size and statistical interpretation
items.answer: It disappeared after childhood IQ was taken into account
items.explanation: Deary reported that people who drank more were already likely to have higher cognitive ability. The adjustment challenges a simple interpretation that drinking produced the apparent benefit.

items.prompt: What caution did Greenwood add to the Lothian findings?
options: Early IQ completely predetermines later mental function and rules out benefits from subsequent experience
Cognitive training has already been established as a universal cure for dementia
Learning can influence cognition only before people leave primary school
The importance of early IQ leaves room for useful interventions
items.answer: The importance of early IQ leaves room for useful interventions
items.explanation: She described cognitive-training research as still at an early stage, while noting growing evidence that improving specific abilities may benefit reasoning and problem-solving.

items.prompt: Which pattern was reported across the decade of repeated cognitive testing?
options: Memory and knowledge held up relatively well, while speed-related abilities declined
Memory, knowledge, abstract reasoning, and reaction speed all improved by the same amount
Processing speed was fully preserved, but accumulated verbal knowledge disappeared
Abstract problem-solving improved steadily while every measure of memory deteriorated
items.answer: Memory and knowledge held up relatively well, while speed-related abilities declined
items.explanation: The article reports some decline in abstract problem-solving, fast thinking, and reaction time. Familiarity with repeated tests may partly explain the comparatively stable memory and knowledge scores.

items.prompt: Why did Deary emphasize individual divergence as well as cohort averages?
options: Every participant's score converged to the same level, regardless of age or initial ability
There were no repeated measurements left from which to estimate a cohort mean
Averages can conceal increasingly different individual trajectories
Each participant completed only one assessment, making individual change unobservable
items.answer: Averages can conceal increasingly different individual trajectories
items.explanation: Scores spread out as participants reached their seventies and eighties. The mean therefore does not fully describe the variation that Deary wanted to explain.

items.prompt: What does diffusion tensor imaging track in the account of brain connectivity?
options: Water movement through white matter tracts
Blood pressure changes during cognitive testing
Childhood school grades reconstructed from adult MRI scans
Family income inferred from the thickness of the cortex
items.answer: Water movement through white matter tracts
items.explanation: The technique was used to examine the integrity of neuronal connections. Roughly 10% of the differences in general cognitive function were linked to connection integrity in this account.

items.prompt: Which statement about white matter hyperintensities matches the article?
options: They occur in exactly equal amounts in everyone, independent of age, health, and living conditions
They consistently decrease in number as people grow older
Their causes and cognitive consequences are fully established
They generally increase with age but vary greatly among individuals
items.answer: They generally increase with age but vary greatly among individuals
items.explanation: Hyperintensities signal damage, but their causes, differing cognitive consequences, and individual susceptibility remained under investigation. A reported link with cortisol does not settle causation.

items.prompt: What alternative interpretation did Karama's cortical-thickness finding suggest?
options: A thinner cortex in old age always indicates an imaging error rather than a biological difference
Childhood IQ and later cortical thickness cannot be statistically associated in any sample
The cerebral cortex never changes during normal aging
Some later differences may reflect less gray matter from the outset
items.answer: Some later differences may reflect less gray matter from the outset
items.explanation: People with a relatively thinner cortex in old age also had lower IQ in childhood. This suggests a possible longstanding difference; it does not demonstrate that cortical shrinkage never occurs.

items.prompt: In the water tank hypothesis, what does starting with a fuller tank represent?
options: Greater cognitive reserve that takes longer to deplete
Drinking more water directly increases brain volume and prevents cognitive decline
Brain volume rises at a constant annual rate throughout adulthood, eliminating neurodegeneration
Genes, early environments, and life experiences have no part in cognitive aging
items.answer: Greater cognitive reserve that takes longer to deplete
items.explanation: The metaphor proposes that a better initial brain endowment, attributed to genes and partly to a favorable early environment, provides more reserve to withstand loss. It is an explanatory hypothesis.

items.prompt: Why does the article emphasize very large samples for research on genetic influences on the brain?
options: DNA cannot be collected from individual participants
Cognitive tests cannot be used in genetic research
Detecting variant effects and gene-environment interplay requires substantial statistical power
Every genetic variant has the same large, easily observed effect
items.answer: Detecting variant effects and gene-environment interplay requires substantial statistical power
items.explanation: The researchers describe needing hundreds of thousands of DNA samples to make even modest progress on variant effects and their interactions with environmental influences.

items.prompt: Which description matches ENIGMA's institutional scale in the 2014 article?
options: 70 institutions in 3 countries
33 participants in 70 countries
1,641 participants in a single country
70 institutions in 33 countries
items.explanation: The article reports that the Lothian studies joined this international consortium in 2009. These figures describe the article's historical account, not the consortium's current membership.
items.source: ENIGMA in the article's historical context

items.prompt: What did McGowan do in response to confronting her own cognitive aging?
options: She stopped painting, studying, and all other daily activities after hearing about the research
She returned to painting and began online university courses at 75
She asked researchers to destroy her childhood records and all follow-up measurements
She withdrew from every subsequent cognitive assessment
items.answer: She returned to painting and began online university courses at 75
items.explanation: The closing account presents her decision to act through art and learning. This personal example does not establish that those activities prevented cognitive decline.

items.prompt: Which output of the Lothian follow-up studies was reported by 2014?
options: Over 250 publications and over 20,000 hours of cognitive tests and brain scans
One clinical trial in which every participant received a new assessment each month
A confirmed dementia diagnosis for every person who took part in either cohort
A complete replacement of childhood test records with retrospective self-reports
items.answer: Over 250 publications and over 20,000 hours of cognitive tests and brain scans
items.explanation: The article describes more than 250 publications and more than 20,000 hours of tests and scans, conducted at roughly two- to three-year intervals. These are cumulative research outputs, not evidence from a randomized intervention.
